reference.title: Red Hat Quay configuration fields updates and changes
reference.shortdesc: You can review configuration fields that are new or changed in Red Hat Quay 3.18, including OIDC multi-issuer settings, QuayRegistry TLS fields, and programmatic bootstrap options.

section.title: SSL_PROTOCOLS and SSL_CIPHERS Operator inheritance on OpenShift Container Platform
section.p: When you deploy Red Hat Quay on OpenShift Container Platform, the Operator can populate the existing SSL_PROTOCOLS and SSL_CIPHERS fields from the cluster-wide OpenShift Container Platform tlsSecurityProfile when neither field is set in the configBundleSecret resource. To fully override or preserve TLS behavior, set both fields. Setting either field disables cluster-profile inheritance for both fields.
For more information, see OpenShift Container Platform cluster TLS security profile inheritance and Preserving TLS settings before upgrading Red Hat Quay on OpenShift Container Platform.

section.title: OIDC multi-issuer and multi-audience fields
section.p: The following optional fields were added to *_LOGIN_CONFIG blocks in Red Hat Quay 3.18:

entry.p: Array of String
Accepted issuer URLs for the provider. When set, Red Hat Quay accepts tokens whose iss claim matches any entry. If not set, Red Hat Quay uses the existing OIDC_ISSUER value.
Array of String

Accepted audience values for bearer token and On-Behalf-Of (OBO) flows. When set, Red Hat Quay validates the token aud claim against this list. CLIENT_ID is always implicitly included. If not set, audience validation defaults to CLIENT_ID.
Array of String
Optional whitelist of authorized party (azp) client IDs. When set, only tokens from these client applications are accepted. If not set, all clients are accepted.

section.p: If both OIDC_ISSUER and OIDC_ISSUERS are set, OIDC_ISSUERS takes precedence and Red Hat Quay logs a warning.

For field reference details, see OIDC configuration fields. For configuration examples, see Configuring Microsoft Entra ID v2 and multi-issuer OIDC. The following configuration fields have been added to Red Hat Quay 3.18.

section.title: QuayRegistry TLS component fields
section.p: The following fields apply to the tls entry in spec.components of the QuayRegistry CR when deploying Red Hat Quay on OpenShift Container Platform.

entry.p: Object

References an external TLS Secret in the same namespace as the QuayRegistry CRD. Valid only when managed is false. The Secret must be of type kubernetes.io/tls and contain tls.crt and tls.key data keys. The Operator watches the Secret and triggers a rolling restart of Red Hat Quay pods when certificate data changes. Do not use with ssl.cert and ssl.key files in the configBundleSecret.
String
Name of the Kubernetes Secret that stores the TLS certificate and private key.
Status
Reports whether TLS from the configured source (external Secret or config bundle) is valid and applied to the registry deployment.

section.p: For procedures and examples, see Referencing an external TLS Secret for Red Hat Quay on OpenShift Container Platform.

section.title: Programmatic bootstrap configuration fields
section.p: Red Hat Quay 3.18 adds configuration fields for Tech Preview programmatic bootstrap OAuth token provisioning:

entry.p: Boolean
Enables bootstrap token auto-generation on startup. Default: false.
String
Superuser that owns the bootstrap OAuth application and token. Required when the feature flag is enabled.
String
Local filesystem path for the bootstrap token JSON. Default: /var/lib/quay/quay-machine-token.json.
Integer
Bootstrap token lifetime in seconds. Default: 3600.
String
Space-separated OAuth scopes for the bootstrap token.
String
Kubernetes Secret name for bootstrap token storage.
String
Secret data key for the bootstrap token JSON. Default: token.json.
String
Namespace for the bootstrap token Secret.

section.p: For descriptions and YAML examples, see Programmatic bootstrap configuration fields.
